lines.en: I walk into the bar to find absolutely no one- a small but noticeable change from last time.
I'm not really sure if this can be chalked up purely to me showing up late, either, considering Sana's already informed me of the struggling state of this business-
But maybe it's even worse off than I thought?
At the bare minimum, there should be at least one customer half-passed out behind the counter, silently drinking to him- or, sorry, herself.
I'm still not fully used to the idea of there not really being any men around here yet, I guess.
: Umm...Hi, Sensei...
: Hey, Sana. Where is everybody?
: This...is everybody...
: Weekdays...aren’t really that busy for us...
: Weekends...aren’t really that busy for us...
: Yeah...I can see that.
: Would you mind if I took a seat? I’ve been walking for a while and I’m pretty exhausted.
: O-Oh! Right! I’m...so sorry...I shouldn't have stopped you as soon as you walked in...
: It’s fine. You were probably just so excited to see another human lifeform in here that you couldn't help but approach me as soon as the door opened.
: What's...really sad is that...you're probably not wrong...
: Is it...okay if I sit next to you, though?...
: What if another customer shows up, though?
: I...don’t really think we have to worry about that...
: I was...probably just going to close down soon anyway, so...
: Then, sure. I don’t mind at all.
: It might be a good time to start your lessons anyway.
: As...good a time as any, I guess...
Sana leads me over to the bar and politely pulls out a stool for me despite it being larger than her and probably weighing twice as much.
She may not have much faith in the business, but at least she's attentive when it comes to customers.
Or at least me.
To be fair, though, there haven’t been many opportunities to see how she acts around others.
I kick off the lesson by remaining completely silent and just observing how Sana acts around me.
And, if she had the confidence in herself to even look my way, she'd be made immediately aware of how creepy and unacceptable this method is.
Unfortunately for her, her inability to make eye contact has already resulted in her missing out on a valuable lesson.
Here's hoping she's at least tried practicing in some way during my absence.
: So, any progress on your end lately? Have you been able to hold any conversations with anyone you're not directly related to?
: Well...there's Ayane too, but...other than that...not really...
: I’ve been trying...but...
Sana drifts off, as if she's expecting me to fill in the blanks of her inadequacies.
Which, to be fair, I probably could. But me doing the legwork isn't going to help her in any way.
If she's going to improve herself, she first needs to confront her problems head on.
: But what?
: It’s just...kind of hard without anyone to talk to...
: I guess that's fair.
: Maybe try practicing in the mirror or something? Isn't that what actors do when they're first starting out?
: Does that...actually work?...
: Maybe. I've never tried. Just...pretend you’re someone else and try to strike up a conversation while...playing both sides?
: That sounds...way too complicated...
: Plus...I don’t really like mirrors...so...
: Why not?
: It's...kind of personal, so...if you don't mind...
: Don't worry about it, then. We can just keep going like this.
I can't blame Sana for not wanting to just freely divulge personal information to me now that we're talking somewhat regularly.
No one should trust anyone until they're given a reason to- and I am no exception to that.
Sana needs time to grow.
Mentally, at least. Because, to be quite honest, I hope she stays her current size forever.
: Here's an idea, Sana. How about we try a little roleplay?
: Roleplay?...You mean like...a game?
: Sure. You can call it a game if you want. Just pretend I’m a customer and-
: Well, actually, I am a customer. But I’m sure you know where I’m going with this.
: Uh...yeah...if...if it's just a game...I can...probably do it...
: Just to mix things up, though, I’m going to try and be difficult. Got it?
: Difficult? How so?
: I mean that I’m going to give you problems that might arise at the bar and you’re going to need to figure out what to do about them.
: You’re not...going to break anything...are you?
: Because...it comes out of my paycheck if you do...
: First off, no. Second, do you really have to pay for things that break on your shift here?
: Well...no...But I’d...feel really bad if I didn’t...
: Not having customers means my mom doesn't have much money, and...I wouldn't want her to pay for all of that out of pocket...
: So...if I can help by...paying for a few broken glasses...I don't really mind...
I guess this means I can assume Sana’s dad isn’t in the picture either.
Is it really just Sana and her mom trying to keep this place afloat on their own? No wonder why they're going under.
There's only so much two people can do- especially when it comes to maintaining a place like this.
: Okay. Well, I promise to not break anything. I’ll just act kind of rude toward you or something.
: Will you be able to handle that?
: Well...can you tell me how rude you’re going to be?
: Nope.
: But-
: Sana, hurry up and get behind the bar. This is a trial by fire.
: But...our extinguisher is...really old and...I don't know if it still works...
: I'm going to ignore that extreme safety hazard for now and say it again. Get behind the bar.
: Okay, but...I can already tell...I'm going to fail whatever this is...
Sana gets out of her seat and nervously rounds the corner into the bar area...
She closes her eyes and takes a deep breath, though I'm not sure how much benefit it will have since I don't intend to pull any punches with this.
: Umm...Hello, sir...What can I-
: Yeah, whatever. Give me a beer and a plate of spaghetti.
: A plate of...spaghetti?...
: Did I stutter? Or are you just really fucking bad at your job?
: Well...I don't think so...but...
: Listen kid, I’m in a hurry. So if you don’t have my spaghetti in five minutes, I’m gonna have to-
: Wait, Sana, are you crying? We literally just started.
: W...w...we...d...don’t...have any...s...sp...spaghetti...
This is even worse than I thought.
: Sana, if this is too hard-
: I’LLGOGETYOURBEER!!!
She scrambles to pick them all up and quickly pulls the first bottle she sees out of the cooler.
: H...Here it is...your...
: Your...
: Ah!
: I’LLBERIGHTBACK!!!
This is hard to watch.
: Don’t laugh at me...
: I’m not laughing. In fact, I feel like I owe you an apology.
: No...You don’t...I’m just not really used to...dealing with pressure...
: No one has ever asked for spaghetti before...I didn’t know how to handle it...
: Well, if it makes you feel any better, I don't think a real customer will ever ask for spaghetti. Especially considering you don't have a menu.
: But, in the event that someone does, it’s always okay to just tell them that you don’t have any.
: B...But when I tried that and you...said...
: What I said doesn't matter.
: I’m sure you’ve heard that whole thing about how the customer is always correct, right?
: Well, that’s not true. In fact, the customer is pretty much always wrong.
: You know this place better than they do, so be assertive and tell me that you don’t have any spaghetti.
: Like...Like right now?...
: Right now.
: Deny me the spaghetti, Sana.
: We don’t have any spaghetti...
: Perfect. That concludes our lesson for the day.
: I’m...so confused...
: Was that...really supposed to help?...
: It probably could have gone a little better on both of our ends. But don't be surprised if you wake up tomorrow and you're suddenly an expert at talking to people.
: Well...at least it was...a little fun?...
: Are you still crying?
: Sana.
: I’ll...try not to freak out next time! I promise!
: And I will try not to make you cry. But, honestly, I'm not sure how much good that's going to do when all it took was spaghetti.
: It was...more the...context of the spaghetti that...made me cry...
: I'm sure it was, Sana.
: I'm sure it was.
Sana and I say our goodbyes and she walks me to the door so she can lock it behind me.
Was today actually successful in teaching her anything?
No.
But, like she said-
At least it was a little fun.
Sana’s affection has increased to [sana_love]!
